definitions.explanation: Reflecting the style, ideas, or technology of the present age. Often used to contrast something with traditional or old-fashioned forms.

examples.japanese: {現代的|げんだいてき}な{建物|たてもの}。
この{店|みせ}は{和食|わしょく}を{現代的|げんだいてき}にアレンジしている。
examples.english: This restaurant gives Japanese cuisine a modern twist.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{考|かんが}え{方|かた}はとても{現代的|げんだいてき}で、{古|ふる}い{習慣|しゅうかん}にとらわれない。
examples.english: Her way of thinking is very modern and not bound by old customs.

notes:
{現代|げんだい} (the present age) + {的|てき} (adjectival suffix). Used as a na-adjective to describe styles, ideas, designs, or attitudes that feel current rather than old-fashioned.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {現代的|げんだいてき}な{デザイン|でざいん}: modern design
- {現代的|げんだいてき}な{感覚|かんかく}: a modern sensibility
- {現代的|げんだいてき}な{解釈|かいしゃく}: a contemporary interpretation
- {現代的|げんだいてき}にアレンジする: to arrange in a modern style

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {伝統的|でんとうてき}: traditional — direct opposite
- {近代的|きんだいてき}: modern (in the historical sense; post-Meiji to mid-20th-century)
- {最新|さいしん}: latest, newest — focuses on novelty rather than overall style
